..
Issued at 316 PM CST Mon Nov 23 2026

Today remains relatively cool with highs only in the 
upper 30s-mid 40s as clouds have filled into the area. A weak 
pressure gradient at the surface is keeping winds light and 
variable. Upper level flow remains mostly zonal west to east aloft 
though some slight ridging is building over the Plains. Clouds 
sticking around over the area keep temps slightly warmer than last 
night, though temps dip down into the mid-20s so tomorrow will be 
another frosty morning. 

The ridging that was beginning to build over the Plains on Monday 
shifts of to the east as a trough begins digging down through the 
area Tuesday morning. As this feature begins to move into the area, 
it will bring a chance (15-20%) for flurries for our southwestern 
areas, mainly Furnas, Phillips, and Rooks counties. While flurries 
are likely to happen with this system, models have been disagreeing 
on how far north and east the flurries will make it. The HRRR model 
was most optimistic on pushing flurries into the area, however 
the most recent 18Z run has pushed the potential back further 
west now barely clipping our area. Should the flurries make it 
into our area, relatively low moisture content under the cloud 
layer will keep precip light and accumulation more than a light 
dusting is not expected. As the trough continues to dig through 
the plains, winds strengthen slightly out of the south at 10-15 
MPH. Clouds remain broken or overcast over the area which keeps 
high temps down in the low 40s. Overnight lows will again drop 
into the low-to-mid 20s. 

The troughing builds into a upper-level closed low that begins to 
move southeast from the Dakotas overnight Tuesday into Wednesday. As 
this system moves through eastern Nebraska it brings another chance 
for flurries through our eastern areas. However, any flurries will 
be short lived as the dry conveyor belt moves in behind the low. The 
pattern then settles through the weekend, keeping highs in the mid 
50s on Saturday the low which will push the necessary moisture out 
of the area. Most models keep the flurries to the east of our area 
aside from the Euro which brings precip all the way back to Kearney. 
Exact positioning of the upper level low will determine how far west 
flurries will be with the Euro keeping the low further west than the 
other models. However, similarly to Tuesday's flurry potential,
low moisture content under the cloud layer will keep 
accumulations to a minimum. Fortunately, holiday travel impacts 
are not expected from this system. As the dry-converyor belt 
moves through, the clouds will also begin to clear behind the 
low. High temps remain in the low-to-mid 40s but with clouds 
clearing and light winds, low temps drop into the upper teens. 

As the low begins to move off to the east-southeast on Thursday
a more zonal pattern forms behind it on Friday. On Thursday, 
the pressure gradient remains relatively weak leading to light 
surface winds. Additionally skies remain with few to scattered 
clouds letting temps warm into the mid 40s with lows dropping 
back to the mid 20s. Precipitation is not expected on Thursday 
or Fridays as the upper level flow keeps dry continental air 
over the central plains. As the trough exits to the east, the 
pressure gradient sharpens slightly bringing stronger winds out 
of the west-northwest in the 10-15 MPH range. Synoptic scale 
descent bringing air down from the Rockies and High Plains warms
the air adiabatically and jumps high temps up into the mid-50s 
on Friday. The upper-level zonal patten continues through the 
weekend, though shortwaves through this pattern could bring our 
next chance for precipitation. Models don't have a consensus on 
the possibility of precip as of right now, however the Euro is 
the most aggressive for precip on Saturday and Sunday. Compared 
to the other models, the Euro brings in a stronger shortwave 
which would give a better chance for widespread precip where the
GFS keeps a more zonal pattern. High temps stay in the mid-50s 
on Saturday before some upper level height falls on Sunday drop 
highs slightly into the upper 40s-mid 50s on Sunday and Monday.
